page.title: Ethernet Status
page.description: Monitor the host ethernet link and configure its negotiated speed.

strip.label: Link state
strip.unavailable_body: Retrying every 10 seconds. Nothing has been changed.
strip.absent_body: This device has no eth0 port, so there is nothing to report or configure.

link.label: Link state
link.caption_up: Cable connected to the host port
link.caption_down: No cable detected on the host port

settings.title: Link speed limit
settings.description: Force the host port to a fixed speed instead of letting it negotiate one.
settings.consequence: Applying drops the link for about 8 seconds while the PHY renegotiates. You are on that link.
settings.consequence_applying: The link is down while the PHY renegotiates. This page will confirm the new rate itself.
settings.consequence_unresponsive: The modem stopped answering, so this control is held until the next successful read.
settings.consequence_unread: The modem hasn't answered yet, so there is nothing to change until the first read lands.
settings.consequence_absent: There is no ethernet port to configure on this device.
settings.provenance: Saved to the modem. Read back from:
settings.toast_confirm_error: Couldn't confirm the new speed. Check the link.

profile_override.banner: {{controls}} is managed by the {{profile_name}} Custom SIM Profile.

login.session_expired: The device was unreachable for too long. Log in again to continue.

recovery.intro: If you've lost the admin password, you have two recovery paths:
recovery.option_reset: Open an SSH session to the device and run {{command}} to set a new admin password. (Requires SSH access to be enabled.)
recovery.option_backup: If you saved a .qmbackup file, re-flash the device firmware and restore from it.

login.locked_body: Locked for {{seconds}} to protect the device.

empty.title: Modem status unavailable
empty.subtitle: The modem has not reported in for a minute. It may be rebooting — the reading resumes on its own.

stale.banner: Readings are <age>{{age}}</age> old. The device may be busy.

unreachable.banner: The modem isn't responding right now. It may be busy or restarting.

sim_swap.title: New SIM card detected
sim_swap.description_no_match: No saved profile matches this SIM.
sim_swap.toast_dismissed: Alert turned off for this SIM
sim_swap.toast_dismissed_detail: Other SIMs still raise the new-SIM alert. Turn this one back on in System Settings → Tracked SIMs.
sim_swap.toast_dismiss_failed: Couldn't turn off the alert for this SIM

dismiss_dialog.title: Stop alerting for this SIM?
dismiss_dialog.description: QManager will stop showing the new-SIM alert for this {{carrier}} SIM only. Every other SIM still raises the alert, and you can turn this one back on any time from System Settings → Tracked SIMs.

page.title: TTL & MTU
page.description: Rewrite the hop count and packet size the modem puts on the cellular interface.

strip.label: In force on rmnet
strip.unavailable_body: Neither endpoint answered. Nothing on the modem has been changed.
strip.idle_body: The modem is using the carrier's TTL and MTU exactly as negotiated. Turn one on below to change that.

banner.title: TTL and hop limit come from the {{profile}} profile
banner.body: Activating that profile writes both values, so this card is held to stop the two writers fighting. Change them in the profile, or activate a profile that leaves TTL unset.

ttl.title: TTL & Hop Limit
ttl.description: Applied to outbound packets on the cellular interface.
ttl.provenance: Read from the live packet rules, replayed at boot from

mtu.title: Maximum transmission unit
mtu.description: The largest packet the cellular interface will send without fragmenting.

shared.consequence_off: Turn the rewrite on to set a value.
shared.consequence_unread: The modem hasn't answered, so there is nothing to change yet.

rewrite.label: Rewrite the hop count
rewrite.consequence: Off means the modem forwards whatever hop count the client sent. Some carriers count hops to detect tethering.

ttl_value.label: TTL value
ttl_value.consequence: {{min}}–{{max}}. A device one hop behind the modem usually wants 64.

hl_value.label: Hop limit value
hl_value.consequence: The IPv6 equivalent. Set both unless you know the client is single-stack.

mtu_toggle.label: Override the MTU
mtu_toggle.consequence: Off restores the carrier-negotiated value on every rmnet_data interface.

mtu_value.label: MTU value
mtu_value.consequence: {{min}}–{{max}}. Below roughly 1400 can break path-MTU discovery on sites that drop ICMP.
mtu_value.consequence_off: Turn the override on to set a value.

errors.value_range: TTL and hop limit must each be between {{min}} and {{max}}.
errors.no_value: Enter a TTL or a hop limit before applying.

ttlMtu.toast_ttl_cleared: The modem is back on the carrier's own hop count.
ttlMtu.toast_ttl_error: Couldn't apply the TTL and hop limit.
ttlMtu.toast_mtu_applied: MTU set to {{mtu}} on every rmnet_data interface.
ttlMtu.toast_mtu_cleared: MTU is back to the carrier-negotiated value.

page.title: Custom DNS
page.description: Choose which resolver the modem forwards LAN queries to. Clients keep querying the modem; only the upstream changes.

strip.label: Currently forwarding
strip.unavailable_title: dnsmasq is not in the path
strip.unavailable_body: DNS mode is {{mode}}, so LAN clients resolve directly against the carrier and nothing on this page can change that.
strip.read_failed_body: The modem did not answer the last read. Nothing on the device has changed — use Refresh to try again.

upstream.caption_untrusted: May not be what dnsmasq is using

corrupt.title: QManager's block in dnsmasq.conf looks malformed
corrupt.body: A begin marker without its end, or the reverse. The upstream list below may not reflect what dnsmasq is actually using. Check /etc/data/dnsmasq.conf over SSH before saving.

unavailable.title: DNS mode is {{mode}}, not PROXY
unavailable.body: The mode lives in /etc/data/mobileap_cfg.xml and has to be changed outside QManager. Until it reads PROXY, saving here would have no effect.

card.title: Upstream resolvers
card.description: Up to four. dnsmasq is reloaded in place — no reboot, no dropped link.
card.provenance_corrupt: {{used}} of {{max}} used · could not be read cleanly from
card.blocked_unavailable: dnsmasq is not in the path, so this would have no effect.

enabled.label: Use my own resolvers
enabled.consequence: Off returns dnsmasq to whatever the carrier handed out on the last attach.

resolver.label: Resolver {{n}}
resolver.consequence: IPv4 or IPv6. Paste a comma-separated list to fill several rows at once.
resolver.consequence_off: Turn custom resolvers on to add one.

ignore_carrier.label: Never fall back to carrier DNS
ignore_carrier.consequence: On, a lookup fails outright when your resolvers are unreachable rather than leaking to the carrier.

errors.invalid_address: Not a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address.
errors.fix_rows: Fix the highlighted resolvers before saving.
errors.empty_when_enabled: Add a resolver, or turn custom resolvers off.

customDns.toast_saved: Custom DNS applied. LAN clients may see a brief pause as caches refresh.

page.title: IP Passthrough
page.description: Hand the modem's public IP straight to one connected device instead of routing for the whole LAN.

mode.label: Mode
mode.caption_eth: Set to hand the WAN IP to eth0
mode.caption_usb: Set to hand the WAN IP to the USB device

nat.label: NAT
nat.caption_off: The target device handles its own public addressing

dns.label: DNS proxy
dns.caption_on: The modem answers DHCP DNS for the target device
dns.caption_off: The target device uses its own resolver

card.title: Passthrough configuration
card.description: Every setting here takes effect on the next boot. Applying reboots the modem.

mode.label: Mode
mode.consequence: Ethernet or USB hands the WAN IP to one device. In either, the modem stops being reachable at its LAN gateway address — keep Tailscale or another way in.

target.label: Target device
target.consequence: Automatic takes the first device that connects; manual pins one MAC address.

nat.label: NAT
nat.consequence: With NAT is right for almost every setup. Without it the target device must handle its own public addressing.

usb.label: USB connection mode
usb.consequence: Only used by USB passthrough. ECM works everywhere; RNDIS is for older Windows.

dns.label: DNS proxy
dns.consequence: On, the modem answers DHCP DNS queries for the target device. Leave off unless the device cannot reach a resolver itself.

options.dns_off: Off — the device uses its own resolver
options.dns_on: On — the modem answers DHCP DNS

reboot.title: Applying reboots the modem, and this browser tab will lose it
reboot.body: After the reboot the LAN gateway stops answering. Reach the modem over Tailscale, from the passthrough device itself, or over serial. The setting persists across further reboots.

active.title: This page is reachable because you are not the passthrough device
active.body: The modem's LAN gateway address is no longer served to {{mac}}. If you lose your current route in, Tailscale or a serial console is the way back.

dialog.title: Apply and reboot now?
dialog.body: The settings are written and the modem reboots immediately. This page hands off to the reboot countdown and signs you out.
dialog.body_gateway: Once passthrough is active the modem stops answering at its LAN gateway address. Make sure you have Tailscale, the passthrough device itself, or a serial console to get back in.
dialog.body_persist: The setting persists across further reboots.

ipPassthrough.toast_apply_error: Couldn't apply the IP Passthrough settings

errors.read_body: Nothing has been changed. Try again, or check that the modem is answering.
errors.card_unread: The modem hasn't answered yet, so there is nothing to change until the first read lands.
errors.mac_invalid: Enter a full MAC address — six pairs of hex digits.

page.title: Traffic Engine
page.description: Bypass ISP DPI throttling of video streaming and other traffic with the built-in bypass engine.

strip.label: Live state
strip.stale_body: The last poll didn't answer. The figures below are held from the previous read, and the engine keeps doing whatever it was doing.
strip.unavailable_body: The modem didn't answer. The engine keeps running whatever it was doing. This is a reporting failure, not an outage.

mode.title: Bypass mode
mode.description: One mode owns the engine at a time. Switching restarts it.
mode.off_hint: No traffic is redirected. The engine stops and the rule is removed.
mode.video_optimizer_hint: Only connections matching your target list. Subdomains match too.
mode.full_bypass_hint: Every TCP 80/443 connection. No target list, so nothing to configure.

takeover.title: Switch to {{mode}}?
takeover.description: Switching modes restarts the engine, which briefly drops every connection going through it.

targets.title: Optimizer targets
targets.description: Domains the engine desyncs. Saved changes apply immediately, with no restart.
targets.idle_title: Not in use while Full Bypass is on
targets.idle_body: Full Bypass desyncs every connection, so there is no list to match against. Your {{count}} saved domains are kept and apply again the moment you switch back to Video Optimizer.
targets.idle_body_empty: Full Bypass desyncs every connection, so there is no list to match against. Anything you add here applies again the moment you switch back to Video Optimizer.

hostlist.empty: No domains yet. Add one to get started.
hostlist.invalid: Enter a valid domain (letters, digits, dots, dashes).
hostlist.duplicate: This domain is already in the list.
hostlist.limit: The list can hold at most 300 domains.
hostlist.too_long: A domain can be at most {{max}} characters.
hostlist.import_too_large: That file is too large. Pick a target list under {{limit}} KB.
hostlist.import_unreadable: That file could not be read.
hostlist.import_invalid_one: 1 line was not a valid domain.
hostlist.import_dropped_one: 1 did not fit under the {{max}} domain limit.
hostlist.import_dropped_other: {{count}} did not fit under the {{max}} domain limit.
hostlist.restore_body_one: This replaces the 1 domain you have saved. Export the list first if you want to keep it.
hostlist.restore_body_other: This replaces the {{count}} domains you have saved. Export the list first if you want to keep them.
hostlist.restore_body_empty: The target list is empty, so nothing of yours is replaced.

verify.title: Test bypass
verify.description: Run a two-phase speed test (without the engine, then with it) plus a speedtest.net reference, to separate CDN throttling from a slow connection.
verify.progress: Downloading the same file twice: once direct, once through the engine. This takes a few minutes.
verify.timeout: The test did not finish in time.
verify.error: The test could not be started
verify.footnote: Line speed is the reference: a slow result on all three is a slow connection, not throttling.

forceTcp.title: QUIC → Force TCP
forceTcp.description: Blocks QUIC (UDP 443) so apps like YouTube and Discord fall back to HTTPS over TCP, where the engine's bypass can apply.
forceTcp.label: Force QUIC over TCP
forceTcp.hint: Applies immediately. Works with either mode, and with neither.
forceTcp.caveat: Can stream slower: if your network already delivers QUIC at full speed, forcing it to TCP adds latency (plus the bypass hop). Enable when QUIC video is throttled or unreliable.

uninstall.title: Uninstall engine binary?
uninstall.description: This action stops the Traffic Engine (if running) and removes the engine binary. Are you sure you want to proceed? It can be reinstalled at a later time if you change your mind.

onboarding.heading: The bypass engine isn't installed yet
onboarding.body: QManager downloads a small engine binary and verifies it against a pinned checksum before installing. It starts on its own once installed.
onboarding.installing_body: Verifying the download against the release manifest and the pinned checksum. This takes about a minute on a normal connection.

page.description: Everything the poller noticed about the radio and the link, newest first.

log.description_unreadable: No counts to show while the log cannot be read.
log.description: Showing {{shown}} of the {{held}} events served, out of the {{cap}} the modem holds in memory.

empty.filtered_description: No events of this kind are in the log right now. Pick All to see everything the poller recorded.

cell.attemptNote: Channel is not set up yet

coverage.outageNoticeWith: An outage would pass silently. Make {{channels}} live to be told.
coverage.outageNoticeNone: An outage would pass silently. No channel on this device can report one.
coverage.staleNotice: Showing the settings we last read from the device.
coverage.errorDesc: The device did not answer, so we cannot show what will fire.
coverage.emptyDesc: The device did not report any alert capabilities, so there is nothing to switch on here.
coverage.unsavedNotice: These ticks are not saved yet. Save them in Channels below.

channels.title: Channels
channels.description: Set up how each one reaches you.

sms.switch_on: Texted over the cellular network, so they still arrive during an outage.
sms.phone_hint: Include the country code with a leading plus.
sms.phone_error: Enter a number with its country code, like +14155551234.
sms.phone_missing: A recipient phone number is required.

email.switch_on: Emailed through Gmail once the connection is back.
email.sender_hint: The Gmail account that sends the alert.
email.password_hint: Generate an app password for this device in your Google Account.
email.password_keep: Leave blank to keep the saved password
email.password_missing: An app password is required to send email.
email.mailer_missing: The msmtp mailer is not installed, so email cannot be sent yet. SMS and Discord still save.

discord.switch_on: Sent as a direct message from your bot once the connection is back.
discord.id_hint: Turn on Developer Mode, right-click your name, then choose Copy User ID.
discord.id_error: Enter a numeric Discord user ID of 17 to 20 digits.
discord.id_missing: An owner Discord ID is required.
discord.token_hint: Create a bot and copy its token in the Discord Developer Portal.
discord.token_keep: Leave blank to keep the saved token
discord.token_missing: A bot token is required to send Discord alerts.

channels.threshold_hint: This channel sends only when the whole outage lasted at least this long. Every channel measures the same outage against its own wait.
channels.threshold_error: Enter a whole number of minutes from 1 to 60.

test.failed: The test could not be sent.
test.blocked_off: Turn this channel on, then save, to send a test.
test.blocked_incomplete: Finish setting this channel up, then save, to send a test.
test.blocked_mailer: Install the msmtp mailer to send a test email.
test.blocked_offline: The Discord bot is not connected yet.
test.blocked_dirty: Save your changes first. A test runs against the saved settings.

save.failed: The settings could not be saved.

empty.description: This device did not return any alert channels, so there is nothing to configure yet.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: Whether this modem joins the tailnet, and how it behaves once it does.
connection.logoutDialogDescription: This removes the modem from your tailnet. You will need to sign in again before it can reconnect.
connection.authDescription: Open the login page and authenticate with your Tailscale account. The modem joins the tailnet as soon as you approve it.
connection.authWaiting: Waiting for you to sign in
connection.bootDescription: Bring Tailscale up automatically after the modem restarts.
connection.sshDescription: Let tailnet members open an SSH session to this modem, subject to your admin-panel ACLs.
connection.sshPending: Pending — this applies the next time the modem connects.
connection.sshLocked: Connect to Tailscale to change this.
connection.sshDialogDescription: Tailnet members will be able to SSH into this modem based on your Tailscale admin-panel ACLs. Review that policy first, so only the people you intend can reach the device.

device.title: This device

device.emptyDescription: Connect Tailscale and this modem's address, DNS name and relay appear here.

peers.title: Network peers

peers.offlineDescription: Connect Tailscale to see the other devices on your tailnet.

install.title: Tailscale
install.description: A mesh VPN for reaching this modem from anywhere, without opening a port.
install.conditionDescription: Installing downloads the Tailscale packages over the same cellular link this session is running on, so it uses your data allowance and the connection will be slower while it runs.

danger.title: Remove Tailscale

danger.dialogDescription: This removes the Tailscale packages, its firewall rules, and all connection state from this modem. A reboot afterwards clears anything left behind.
danger.rebootDescription: Tailscale has been removed. Rebooting clears the leftover firewall rules and other artifacts. Reboot now?

page.title: Watchdog
page.description: Watches the internet link and climbs a recovery ladder when it goes down.
page.unreadableTitle: Could not read the watchdog settings

band.rebootsCaption: Safety cap, counted since the watchdog started
band.rebootsOff: The reboot step is off, so the cap cannot fire

off.label: Off
off.blurb: The watchdog is not watching the connection.

unknown.label: Unknown
unknown.blurb: The modem is not answering, so we cannot say what the watchdog is doing.

starting.label: Starting
starting.blurb: The service was just enabled and has not reported yet.

not_running.label: Not reporting
not_running.blurb: Enabled, but the service has not reported since boot.

auto_disabled.label: Turned itself off
auto_disabled.blurb: The reboot limit was reached, so the watchdog switched itself off.

monitor.label: Monitoring
monitor.blurb: The connection is healthy. Watching for outages.

suspect.label: Checking
suspect.blurb: A connectivity check just failed. Confirming before acting.

recovery.label: Recovering
recovery.blurb: Working through the recovery ladder to restore the connection.

cooldown.label: Cooling down
cooldown.blurb: Waiting for the last recovery step to settle before rechecking.

locked.label: Paused
locked.blurb: Maintenance is in progress, so the watchdog is holding off.

disabled.label: Disabled
disabled.blurb: The service is running but switched off.

master.title: Connection watchdog
master.description: Watch the link and recover it automatically. Applies when you save.

ladder.title: Recovery ladder
ladder.description: Tried in order, gentlest first. Each step runs only if the one before it did not bring the link back.

tier1.name: Re-register to the network
tier1.effect: Detaches from the carrier and attaches again.
tier1.consequence: The link drops for a few seconds. Nothing else is affected.

tier2.name: Restart the radio
tier2.effect: Turns the radio off and back on.
tier2.consequence: Skipped automatically while a tower lock is active, so your locked cells survive.

tier3.name: Switch to the backup SIM
tier3.effect: Fails over to the other SIM slot and rides on it.
tier3.consequence: Without a backup slot the ladder stops here and never reaches the reboot step.
tier3.slotHint: The slot the watchdog switches to. Your primary SIM stays in the other one.

tier4.name: Reboot the device
tier4.effect: Restarts the modem as a last resort.
tier4.consequence: This page goes away for about a minute while the modem comes back.
tier4.capHint: How many reboots are allowed in an hour. At the cap the watchdog switches itself off.

detection.title: Detection
detection.description: How quickly a quiet link counts as an outage.

probe.label: Probe interval
probe.hint: How often the modem probes the internet to confirm it is reachable.

threshold.label: Failure threshold
threshold.hint: How many probes in a row must fail before recovery begins.

cooldown.label: Cooldown (seconds)
cooldown.hint: How long to wait after each recovery step before checking the connection again.

derived.ready: Declares the connection down after about {{seconds}}s of failed probes.
derived.unavailable: Enter valid detection values to preview when the connection is declared down.

activity.title: Recovery activity
activity.description: What the watchdog has done, newest first.

empty.title: No recovery activity yet
empty.description: Recovery steps and SIM failovers appear here when the watchdog acts on an outage. Older activity ages out of the modem event log.

save.toastFail: Could not save the watchdog settings

confirmReboot.title: Let the watchdog reboot the modem?
confirmReboot.body: Saving this lets the watchdog restart the modem on its own when every gentler step has failed.
confirmReboot.cap: Reboots are capped at {{cap}} per hour. If it reaches that cap it switches the whole watchdog off — monitoring included — until you turn it back on.

errors.backupSim: Choose a backup SIM slot to enable failover

autoDisabled.title: The watchdog turned itself off
autoDisabled.description: It reached the reboot limit for this hour. Re-enable it once the connection is stable.

failover.title: Running on the backup SIM
failover.body: Switched to slot {{current}} {{since}}. The original SIM is in slot {{original}}.
failover.confirmBody: This switches back to SIM slot {{original}}. Your internet will briefly disconnect while the modem reconnects.
failover.requested: SIM revert requested. The watchdog will process it shortly.
failover.failed: Could not request the SIM revert
